slides.title: Melanotan I and II aren't the same
slides.text: One is a drug, the other isn't. Swipe 👉

slides.title: FDA-approved
slides.text: As afamelanotide (Scenesse), the FDA approved it in October 2019 for adults with erythropoietic protoporphyria, to increase pain-free light exposure. A 16 mg implant every 2 months, given by a clinician.

slides.title: No approved use
slides.text: Sold illegally as a 'tanning injection.' Its safety has not been established.

slides.title: Different receptors, different risk
slides.text: MT-I selectively targets the MC1R receptor. MT-II also activates MC3R and MC4R, linked to effects like libido and appetite changes, and in case reports to new moles and melanoma.

slides.title: "It's basically the same drug"
slides.text: MT-II sellers sometimes imply it's equivalent to an approved drug. It isn't: only MT-I (afamelanotide) is approved, in a specific form, dose and indication.
A peptide catalog, myths vs. facts, and the FDA decision timeline.

caption:
Melanotan I and Melanotan II are NOT the same 🧪 One is an FDA-approved drug (afamelanotide/Scenesse) for a rare disease. The other is an illegal 'tanning injection' with no established safety.
